rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or Evaluator feedback yet, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Geometry: five sensors spaced 20 mm apart across the centre (x = -0.04 to +0.04) and 50 mm ahead of the axle, so they see the line before the wheels reach it. A 12 mm sensor footprint covers most of the 25 mm tape at any lateral offset. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a moderate turn rate and a reasonable top speed. Mass 0.8 kg with a 0.12 m body width keeps the off-track limit at 0.06 m. Controller: sensor weights run -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 so the signal is a linear lateral error (positive = left, which steers left). kp = 2.5 gives a turn of up to about 5 at full signal, which is a firm correction. kd = 0.15 damps the response to changes in signal. ki = 0 avoids integral windup on curves. base_speed = 1.6 (about 80 percent of full PWM) is a compromise: it should reach the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish within 3 s, while leaving margin to correct on the tighter bends. line_loss = last_direction lets the robot turn back toward the side it last saw the line. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with rms error of a few mm. The slalom is the likely failure point, due to fast direction changes. Hypotheses to test: (1) kp is high enough to track the tighter bends without oscillation; (2) base_speed 1.6 finishes in under 3 s; (3) kd prevents oscillation at this speed. Next race should show whether steering_oscillation is high (kd or kp too large) or max_error grows on the slalom (kp too low, or base_speed too high for the turns).
